experiment: Dynamic per-Sim Simlish voice suppression in pure Python via voice_actor FNV-32 suffix overrides

fa.note: Also the C++ default fallback when voice_actor is assigned 0

key_mechanism_findings.finding: sim_info.voice_actor is the FNV-32 hash of the 2-3 character voice suffix
key_mechanism_findings.detail: When PlaySound(..., is_vox=True) or an animation voice event fires, the client appends the Sim voice suffix (_ma, _mb, _fa, _fd, _cb, etc.) to the cue name before hashing the 64-bit resource ID.

key_mechanism_findings.finding: Assigning 0 to voice_actor triggers a C++ fallback to fa (1802970394), whereas 0x7FFFFFFF (2147483647) stores verbatim and silences vox cues
key_mechanism_findings.detail: In our first test, assigning info.voice_actor = 0 caused _base.voice_actor to reassign 1802970394 (fnv32("fa")). Assigning a non-zero unmapped integer (0x7FFFFFFF = 2147483647) stored 2147483647 verbatim, preserved the true voice_actor (1685527063) in _original_voice_actors for companion TTS selection, and silenced is_vox=True playback.

key_mechanism_findings.finding: Paused clock stops simulation audio channels even when immediate=True
key_mechanism_findings.detail: Under clock.pause, PlaySound(..., immediate=True) produced MaxSessionPeak=0.0 across the entire window.

muted_stepB_banter_mute_on.note: Dropped 10x to the ~0.002-0.004 ambient room floor; no Simlish utterance peak occurred.

limits: Digital session peak suppression was verified while hardware speakers stayed muted overnight; human-ear listening during full social conversations remains to be checked when Max is awake.
Non-vox sound effects (footsteps, objects, ambient audio) remain unaffected by voice_actor.
